label: copy-phase echo of z/t/0/g/q/e (longer sequences)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or the <DEL> step), when the fed-back input is one of a small token set: z, t, 0, g, q, e (each with about 4-5x lift), and more weakly b and m. It is stronger and more frequent in longer sequences (L >= 6; L = 9 holds half the mass) and at absolute steps 9-12. Most mass sits on the second and third copy inputs (prev2_tok = <DEL> holds 35% of mass), but limiting to early copy steps hurts recall. Rarely fires on x, 3, f, 1 or on the last copy step. Precision is only about 0.5-0.6: about half of copy-phase steps with these tokens stay inactive, which suggests a context dependence that no simple variable captures. Dev F1 is 0.62 for the token set alone and 0.67 with L >= 6.
